paragraphs.source_en: Kazumasa believed that even after he was gone, Ieyasu would neither blame Ishikawa Ienari nor mistreat his grandmother, Myōsaini. But if their party were captured in Mikawa, they would certainly be bound to crosses and crucified. If that happened, the grandmother who had taught him the doctrines of Buddhism since childhood would surely be overcome with mortal grief.

paragraphs.source_en: Even now, Kazumasa remained true to his original resolve. Outwardly, he acted from the Buddhist ideal of saving all living beings and struggled for peace throughout the realm; deep in his heart, however, he longed for Ieyasu to win the realm! That simple wish lay buried in the depths of his heart. Now, even if the world regarded him as a villain and a traitor, inwardly he could only laugh heartily.

paragraphs.source_en: For whom was he doing all this? For Tokugawa Ieyasu, of course! Answering his own question, Kazumasa could not keep himself from smiling: At some point, my lord and I became one. Yes, for the sake of the great enterprise, Ishikawa Kazumasa was now leaving Okazaki.
